introduction: A graduation session marks the end of years of work with photographs made on your terms, away from the crowd and the clock of the ceremony. Whether you are finishing high school, college or university, you get time to be photographed in the gown, in your own clothes, and with the people who got you here.
This page explains how a session fits around convocation, what to do about the gown, who can join you and how to book a graduation photographer in London, Ontario.

sections.heading: Before or after the ceremony
body: The first decision is timing. Before the ceremony you are fresh and the gown is crisp, but you may be rushed and nervous. Afterwards you are relaxed and finished, though the gown may need returning, the light has moved on and a hot day has taken its toll. Some graduates choose a separate date near convocation so that nobody is watching the clock. A hired gown often has to go back soon after the ceremony, so check your return date before you decide. [[CONFIRM: the studio's advice on timing, and whether sessions are held before, after or apart from the ceremony]].

sections.heading: Where the session can happen
body: Many people want the campus where they spent the last few years, and a few want somewhere with no connection to school at all. A campus is a rule-bound place: whether a professional session is allowed, where, and whether it needs a permit is decided by the institution and not by the photographer, so ask yours before you plan. The studio photographs graduations at [[CONFIRM: the campuses and places the studio uses; the candidates are Western University, Fanshawe College, Huron University College, King's University College, Brescia University College, Victoria Park, the Thames Valley Parkway, Springbank Park, Gibbons Park and downtown London; also any permit requirement and any travel fee outside London]].

sections.heading: Who joins you
body: Some graduates want a solo session and some want the people who helped: parents, siblings, grandparents, partners and the friends who finished with them. Decide in advance which photographs matter most, whether that is you alone, you with your family or you with your friends. Take the group photographs first, since relatives tire and friends leave, and finish with the portraits of you alone. [[CONFIRM: whether family and friends can join the session, and any group-size limit]].

sections.heading: Booking around convocation
body: Convocation dates belong to the institutions, so look yours up as soon as they are published and work backwards from there. Graduation season is short, which means popular days fill and a late request may find nothing. Think about announcements, gifts and frames too: if you want printed photographs for a party, plan the session early enough to leave time after it. The studio suggests booking [[CONFIRM: how far ahead of convocation to book, and the busiest weeks]].

faqs.question: Should we take graduation photos before or after the ceremony?
faqs.answer: Either works, and the right answer depends on your gown and your nerves. Before the ceremony the gown looks its best but the day is tight; afterwards you are relaxed but may need to give the gown back. A separate date near convocation removes both pressures, provided the gown is yours to keep or can be held.

faqs.question: Do I need to bring my gown and hood?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you want photographs in them, and bring the cap and any stole or cord as well. Pack a change of clothes and comfortable shoes for walking between spots. Iron or steam the gown the night before, because creases show in photographs more than they do in person.

faqs.question: Can my family and friends join the session?
faqs.answer: Often that is the point of the day. If they do join, plan who stands where in advance and keep the group photographs near the start, while everyone is still patient. [[CONFIRM: how many guests can join a session and whether guests affect the starting price]].

faqs.question: Can we shoot on campus?
faqs.answer: Often, but the rule belongs to the campus rather than the photographer, and policies on professional photography differ between institutions. Ask your school's events or communications office whether a permit or a booking is needed, and for which areas. [[CONFIRM: which campuses the studio has shot at and whether the studio arranges any permit]].

faqs.question: When will I get my graduation photographs?
faqs.answer: What you receive in edited and original photographs is set out in the package. Timing matters more than usual in graduation season, because of announcements and gifts. [[CONFIRM: the delivery time and form, and whether photographs can be delivered before a particular date on request]].

faqs.question: What if the weather is bad or my ceremony date changes?
faqs.answer: Rain, heat and a changed ceremony date are all things a graduation session has to survive. If the ceremony moves, tell the studio at once so that the session can move with it. [[CONFIRM: the studio's policy for rain, cold and rescheduling, including what happens when a ceremony date moves]].

faqs.question: How do I book a graduation session?
faqs.answer: Use the contact link below with your institution, your convocation date and the places you have in mind. The package further up gives the starting price and what comes with it, and [[CONFIRM: deposit, cancellation and travel-fee terms]] are explained at booking.
